resources.string: Dictate from your keyboard
Most keyboards have a mic key. Here is how each of your keyboards gets to Marmalade STT.
Turn on the Marmalade voice keyboard first (the previous step): mic keys open it.
Turn off other voice keyboards

Also on: %1$s. Most mic keys open the first voice keyboard that\'s on, and Android puts preinstalled ones first. Turn these off in Android\'s keyboard settings (on most phones Settings → System → Keyboard → On-screen keyboard).
%1$s (in use)
Tap its mic key. It opens the first voice keyboard that\'s on, so keep Marmalade voice typing the only one. No mic key? Look for a voice input key in its settings or toolbar.

Tap its mic key, and keep Marmalade voice typing the only voice keyboard that\'s on. This keyboard can see Marmalade only after you\'ve typed in this app with it: if the mic key is missing or does nothing, type a letter in the box below with it. After restarting your phone, do that again.
Tap its voice key and pick Marmalade voice typing. It remembers your choice.

In Fossify Keyboard\'s settings, set “Voice typing method” to Marmalade voice typing; its toolbar then shows a mic. Fossify can see Marmalade only after you\'ve typed in this app with it: if Marmalade isn\'t in the list, or the mic does nothing, type a letter in the box below with Fossify first. After restarting your phone, do that again.

SwiftKey\'s mic uses Microsoft\'s own voice typing. With “Multi-modal voice typing” turned off (SwiftKey settings → Rich input), it asks Android for speech input instead, which can open Marmalade STT. We haven\'t been able to test this yet.
Its mic key always uses its own voice typing. To use Marmalade instead, tap the keyboard button in the navigation bar and pick Marmalade voice typing.
Its mic key only opens Google voice typing. To use Marmalade instead, tap the keyboard button in the navigation bar and pick Marmalade voice typing.
It has no mic key. To use Marmalade, tap the keyboard button in the navigation bar and pick Marmalade voice typing.
Try its mic key in the box below. Keyboards whose mic key switches to a voice keyboard open Marmalade voice typing; keep it the only voice keyboard that\'s on.
FUTO Keyboard
Try it here
Tap the box, then your keyboard\'s mic key.
Speech recognition for other apps
Some apps have a mic button that uses Android\'s speech recognition service. Pick Marmalade STT as that service, and they recognize your speech on your phone too.
Marmalade STT is Android\'s speech recognition service
Marmalade STT isn\'t Android\'s speech recognition service
Open settings
In Settings, open Apps & notifications → Advanced → Default apps → Assist & voice input → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT. If Voice input isn\'t listed, set Assist app to None first.
In Settings, open Apps & notifications → Advanced → Default apps → Assist app → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT. If Voice input isn\'t listed, set Assist app to None first.

In Settings, open Apps & notifications → Advanced → Default apps → Digital assistant app → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT. If Voice input isn\'t listed, set Default digital assistant app to None first.
In Settings, open Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT.
In Settings, open System → Languages & input → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT.
In Settings, open System → Languages → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT.
In Settings, open System → Language & region → Speech → Voice input, and pick Marmalade STT.
Search Settings for “Voice input”, open it, and pick Marmalade STT.
Some phones keep it elsewhere: search Settings for “Voice input”.
If you force-stop Marmalade STT, Android switches back to another service. Pick Marmalade again then.
